messages:
emily_support: Customer reported an incorrect MA sales tax on their Dedicated invoice despite sending a PO with a government exemption flag. They want a credit and a reissued invoice without tax.

raj_billing: tagging @olivia_finance & @tanya_ops — putting the invoice here. customer says PO included exemption ID and they have a MA Direct Pay permit. :thinking_face:

invoices-bot: Invoice INV-2026-0173 created for acme-analytics (dedicated). Amount: $12,500. Tax: $781.25 (MA 6.25%). PO: PO-5566.

emily_support: customer paste of PO note: "Exempt — MA Direct Pay Permit: DPP-6721. Please do not apply sales tax. Invoice to reference PO-5566." They uploaded PDF in the ticket.

raj_billing: I pulled the invoice JSON from billing-api: 
```
{
  "invoice_id": "INV-2026-0173",
  "bill_to": {"name":"Acme Analytics","address":{"line1":"100 Market St","city":"Boston","state":"MA","zip":"02110"}},
  "po_number": "PO-5566",
  "tax_applied": "MA",
  "tax_rate": "6.25",
  "tax_exempt": false
}
```

raj_billing: The PO flag didn't get propagated into `tax_exempt`. Looks like our invoice generation path ignored PO metadata for Dedicated accounts created via self-serve flow.

emily_support: customer insists they attached the PO to their account on 2026-03-02. They got billed automatically on 2026-03-15.

raj_billing: repro steps from my end: 1) GET /v1/accounts/acme-analytics -> returns billing_profile with `legal_entity` pointing at parent company (Acme Labs) 2) POST /v1/invoices/generate for period -> tax-microservice uses `billing_profile.address` to determine jurisdiction 3) PO metadata stored on account under `purchase_orders` but invoice generator reads `purchase_orders` only for enterprise SKUs, not Dedicated. That's the bug.

raj_billing: quick log excerpt from tax-microservice: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:01:12Z] invoice=INV-2026-0173 account=acme-analytics lookup_jurisdiction(address=100 Market St,02110) -> MA
[2026-03-15T02:01:12Z] invoice=INV-2026-0173 purchase_order_found=false tax_exempt=false
```

olivia_finance: If tax_exempt was true we'd issue zero-rated invoice and not collect sales tax. We need to credit the collected amount and reissue. Can eng confirm that setting `tax_exempt` on invoice is safe for existing accounting flows?

raj_billing: @olivia_finance yes, accounting code paths exist for credit+reissue when `tax_exempt=true`. The runtime will mark the invoice as reversal + replacement. I'll open an internal PR to make invoice generation respect `purchase_orders` metadata for Dedicated accounts.

emily_support: Customer is asking for ETA and proof of correction for procurement. They need a corrected invoice in their AP system by EOD PT tomorrow.

raj_billing: short-term manual fix: finance can create a credit for INV-2026-0173 and issue INV-2026-0173-R with tax_exempt=true. I'll attach the logs and the PO PDF to the credit note for audit.

olivia_finance: I can do the manual credit and reissue once eng confirms the exemption ID. @raj_billing please confirm the PO ID and the permit number we'll include in tax notes.

raj_billing: Confirming: PO-5566, MA Direct Pay Permit DPP-6721. I'll also update the account-level `purchase_orders` flag so future invoices won't hit this.

tanya_ops: Quick ask for ops: can we add a check in the invoicing SLOs to surface mismatches between `purchase_orders` and `billing_profile` before charging? Would avoid surprises.

raj_billing: yes, I'll add a pre-flight validation in the generator. For now, @olivia_finance — proceed with manual credit. I'll follow up with a PR link and a link to the fixed invoice once done. :thumbsup:

emily_support: Thanks all. I'll update the customer that finance will issue credit and replacement and that eng has a patch coming. Will follow up with the replacement invoice ID once available. :eyes:
